formPost.title: Returning to the client
formPost.heading: Returning to the client
formPost.sub: OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode — the authorization response travels in a form POST rather than in a redirect, so it never appears in a URL, in browser history or in a Referer header (RFC 9700 section 4.3).
formPost.scriptNote: The form submits itself from /oauth2/autopost.js. It is a separate resource because this service sets script-src 'none' on every response and this page relaxes it to 'self'; with scripting off the button IS the mechanism.
logout.askAppWho: The application {app} asked to sign you out of {who}. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.askApp: The application {app} asked to sign you out. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.askWho: An application asked to sign you out of {who}. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.ask: An application asked to sign you out. This ends your session here, and every application signed in through it is told.
logout.why: Asked because the request did not prove it came from an application you are signed in to with this session (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 section 2).
signedOut.title: Signed out
signedOut.heading: Signed out
signedOut.ended: The session for {username} has ended, and every application signed in through it is told.
signedOut.none: There was no session to end.
signedOut.frontSub: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0, with Front-Channel Logout 1.0
signedOut.frontEnded: The session for {username} has ended. It is the session WS-Federation and SAML 2.0 share, so those are signed out too.
signedOut.frontNone: There was no session to end. The cookie has been cleared anyway.
signedOut.returnAuto: This page returns there by itself after {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}, once the notifications above have had time to load; the link is for a browser that does not follow a refresh.
signedOut.returnLink: A link and not a redirect: the notifications above load with this page, and a 302 would abandon them before they were sent.
